page: Microsoft Azure M416-208s_v2 is a memory-optimized server belonging to the MSv2 family. It features 208 vCPUs mapped to 104 physical cores on Intel Xeon 8280L processors running at 2.7 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, utilizing Hyper-Threading with 2.0 threads per core. The server is equipped with a massive 5700.0 GB of RAM, providing approximately 27.4 GB of memory per core. It includes 8389 GB of local SSD storage and supports Premium Storage, but does not feature any GPUs.

Benchmark data reveals a significant contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng and single-threaded gzip compression, fall into the bottom 25%. Conversely, multi-core capabilities are top-tier, with stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores ranking in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, reaching 10446.46 GB/sec for cached reads and 651.24 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Redis SET operations also perform in the top 10%, delivering 162.62 million operations per second.

Given its massive memory footprint and high multi-threaded performance, this server is designed for resource-intensive enterprise applications. The qualitative cost profile reflects its position as a high-density, specialized instance where the investment is justified by the extreme memory capacity and parallel processing capabilities rather than single-threaded speed. It is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, massive data warehousing, enterprise relational databases, and heavy multi-threaded simulation workloads.
description: The Microsoft Azure M416-208s_v2 is a high-capacity, memory-optimized server from the MSv2 family. Powered by Intel Xeon 8280L processors, it delivers 208 vCPUs across 104 physical cores with a 2.7 GHz clock speed. The server features an extraordinary 5700.0 GB of RAM alongside 8389 GB of local SSD storage, with no GPU accelerators. While single-core benchmarks are relatively weak, its multi-core and memory performance are top-tier, demonstrated by exceptional memory bandwidth and multi-threaded decompression speeds. This hardware profile is optimized for massive parallel workloads, making it highly suitable for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning systems, and intensive data warehousing operations where memory capacity and multi-core throughput are critical.
